kept.excerpt: A record-breaking 34 candidates are standing in the Clacton by-election after Nigel Farage resigned from the seat, with the intention of running again. Mainstream parties have all refused to field candidates, but a vast array of independents have put forward candidates for Clacton. Clacton will head to the polls on Thursday, August 13.
kept.relevance: This late-July report confirms the scheduled election and the unusually fragmented field against which Binface must finish second.

kept.excerpt: The intergalactic warlord and candidate in the Clacton by-election, Count Binface, has revealed a raft of policies in his official manifesto. MPs who resign mid-parliament to be barred from the resulting by-election. MPs who change party mid-parliament to be forced to face a by-election.
kept.relevance: The dated manifesto report establishes that Binface was actively campaigning near the cutoff and targeting the circumstances that triggered the election.

kept.excerpt: A record number of candidates for a UK parliamentary election have been confirmed for the Clacton constituency by-election. Voters will go to the polls on Thursday, 13 August, to choose who will represent them in Parliament. A total of 34 candidates are standing in the by-election, which is believed to be a record for a parliamentary election.
kept.relevance: The election administrator provides primary-source confirmation of the timetable and the number of competitors relevant to second place.

kept.excerpt: Nigel Farage will compete with a record 33 other candidates in the Clacton by-election, despite several political parties refusing to stand. Labour, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats and the Green Party have all boycotted the by-election and said they will not be putting forward a candidate.
kept.relevance: The absence of the principal established opposition parties materially changes the competition for second place.

kept.excerpt: New polling data from Ipsos in the UK, conducted 8–9 July 2026, explores public attitudes to Nigel Farage’s decision to resign as an MP and force a by-election in Clacton. When asked about the Clacton contest, 1 in 3 British adults (33%) would prefer Count Binface to win, while 21% prefer Nigel Farage and 32% choose neither. 13% don’t know.
kept.relevance: This measures national preference and Binface's public visibility, but is not a poll of Clacton voting intention or a direct estimate of second-place probability.

kept.excerpt: The Chancellor of the Exchequer has this day appointed Nigel Paul Farage to be Steward and Bailiff of the Manor of Northstead.
kept.relevance: This official notice documents the appointment used to vacate Farage's parliamentary seat and establishes the procedural basis for the by-election.

removed.reason: Contains election results, including final placing and vote totals. Although these are historical 2024 results, the stated removal rule excludes excerpts mentioning results.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-07-31 inclusive. Selected only dated sources published by that cutoff; no election outcome, later developments, betting pages, odds, or market prices are included. Publication dates and excerpts were checked against web-search-indexed source text. Direct web_fetch failed because of a provider configuration error; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable. The Ipsos publication date of 2026-07-10 is corroborated by contemporaneous reporting and bibliographic references; its survey covers British adults rather than Clacton constituents. Sources with unverifiable publication dates were omitted.
